'''Jeffrey Henderson Smith''' is a former professor of [[mathematics]] at [[Purdue University]] in [[Lafayette, Indiana]]. He received his Ph.D. from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1981, under the supervision of [[Daniel Kan]],<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Jeffrey Henderson Smith|id=63605}}.</ref> and was promoted to full professor at Purdue in 1999.<ref>[http://www.math.purdue.edu/about/purview/summer99/article04_yearReview.html Math PUrview], Summer 1999, retrieved 2010-01-23.</ref> His primary research interest is [[algebraic topology]]; his best-cited work<ref>[https://scholar.google.com/scholar?as_q=&num=10&btnG=Search+Scholar&as_epq=&as_oq=&as_eq=&as_occt=any&as_sauthors=%22jh+smith%22&as_publication=&as_ylo=&as_yhi=&as_sdt=1&as_subj=eng&as_sdts=5&hl=en Google scholar], accessed 2010-01-23.</ref> consists of two papers in the ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]'' on "nilpotence and stable homotopy".
